rows.name: Constellation Software Inc.
rows.last_memo: Constellation's stock jumped about 6.5% today with no apparent reason — no earnings, no acquisition news, no management update. For a company like this, where what matters is whether management keeps buying good software businesses at attractive prices and compounding free cash f

rows.name: Deckers Outdoor Corp.
rows.last_memo: Deckers had a decent but not exceptional quarter—sales grew about 6%, the direct-to-consumer business (selling straight to shoppers, bypassing retailers) grew a healthy 13%, and international demand kept building. The downside is that spending on overhead and marketing grew much
risks: SG&A growing at 2.2x the rate of revenue in Q1 FY27; if this reflects a higher-cost operating model rather than investment spending, operating margins could structurally compress by 200-300bps versus thesis assumptions.

Inventory rose $320M in the quarter to $807.6M—a seasonal build but the absolute level warrants monitoring against sell-through data; any buildup into fiscal year-end would be a kill-criterion proximity signal.

Operating lease commitments surged ($120M of new ROU assets in one quarter vs. $45M prior year), indicating a significant retail or distribution footprint expansion; lease costs are fixed obligations that increase operating leverage in a downturn.
Tariff uncertainty explicitly mentioned in forward-looking statements; as a footwear company with overseas manufacturing, any sustained tariff escalation could structurally raise COGS.

rows.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
rows.last_memo: Twenty-nine U.S. states have taken Meta to trial arguing that Facebook and Instagram are deliberately designed to be addictive for young users, and the outcomes could include forced changes to how the apps recommend content, notify users, or target teenagers. This is a serious es
risks: Court-ordered redesign of algorithmic recommendation or notification systems for minors could reduce teen engagement and set precedent applicable to broader platform design.
A plaintiff-favorable verdict could trigger federal legislative action or EU copycat proceedings that extend product restrictions beyond the U.S. youth cohort.
Settlement costs, while manageable on Meta's balance sheet, could be large enough to attract attention and signal regulatory vulnerability to other jurisdictions.
Adverse ruling could restrict Meta's ability to use certain engagement-optimization techniques that also benefit adult user experience and advertiser targeting.

rows.name: Microsoft Corporation
rows.last_memo: China's government is speeding up its plan to replace Windows on government computers with Chinese-made software alternatives. This has been happening gradually for years, driven by geopolitics rather than product dissatisfaction. Microsoft doesn't make a lot of money from Chines
risks: Acceleration of sovereign 'de-Americanization' IT policies could set a precedent that other governments (e.g., EU member states, Global South) reference when evaluating Microsoft dependency.
Chinese domestic OS alternatives maturing faster than expected could eventually threaten Microsoft's commercial enterprise position in China, not just government.
If China exits extend to Azure or Microsoft 365 commercial accounts under future policy expansion, the revenue impact would become more material.
An 18% weekly price surge increases the risk that near-term sentiment is now priced for perfection, leaving less margin of safety if Azure growth decelerates even modestly.

rows.name: International Business Machines Corporation
rows.last_memo: IBM just got the federal government's official security seal of approval for a cloud version of its Maximo software, which helps large organizations manage physical assets like equipment and facilities. This matters because U.S. government agencies can now buy Maximo as a subscri
risks: Federal procurement cycles are long and unpredictable; FedRAMP authorization does not guarantee contract wins, and continued cost or DOGE-related federal IT budget pressures could delay or reduce expected government SaaS revenue.

Use of proceeds undisclosed: if this debt funds an acquisition rather than refinancing, it would trigger the kill criterion around value-destructive M&A and push leverage further above our comfort threshold.

Refinancing risk crystallized: rolling 2026 near-zero-coupon notes into 4.1-4.75% paper raises annual interest costs by an estimated $80-95M, modestly reducing FCF generation and slowing the deleveraging path.
Currency mismatch: CAD-denominated debt issued by a primarily USD-reporting company introduces a foreign exchange liability that must be hedged or absorbed, adding a small but real ongoing cost.

rows.name: Amazon Com Inc.
rows.last_memo: Amazon's cloud boss said that essentially all of their AI server capacity is already committed to customers through 2028 — think of it like a hotel where every room is booked years in advance. This is important because one of the biggest questions about Amazon has been whether co
risks: Execution risk on supply side: if Amazon cannot build data center and AI chip capacity fast enough to honor multi-year commitments, customer satisfaction and contract terms could be impaired.

Concentration risk: capacity locked through 2028 means AWS is betting heavily on AI workloads remaining on current architectural assumptions — a disruptive shift in AI compute paradigm (e.g., dramatically more efficient models) could strand infrastructure investment.
Memory price inflation adding ~$20B to the capex program creates a near-term FCF headwind that could persist through 2026-2027 depending on DRAM/HBM market conditions.

Long-term debt doubled from $65.6B to $128.9B in six months (H1 2026 new issuance of ~$67B); while net debt/EBITDA remains well below 2.5x given earnings scale, the leverage trajectory warrants monitoring.

rows.name: Lululemon Athletica Inc.
rows.last_memo: Lululemon's head of AI and technology just left the company, and this comes while the company is already searching for a permanent CEO. Neither leader has been replaced yet. This isn't a catastrophe for the brand or the business — the leggings still sell, the stores still perform
risks: Dual leadership vacuum — no permanent CEO and now no permanent Chief AI & Technology Officer — increases the probability of delayed or inconsistent strategic decisions during a critical execution window.
Incoming permanent CEO may conduct a broader leadership review, creating further turnover risk across the executive team before operational stability is restored.
Technology and AI roadmap uncertainty could slow DTC personalization and supply chain optimization initiatives that underpin inventory discipline and full-price sell-through.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corporation
rows.last_memo: NVIDIA apparently agreed to a slightly smaller guaranteed commitment for a massive data center it is helping OpenAI build in Ohio — the revised guarantee is $120 billion, down from some higher number. To put that in perspective, $120 billion is still one of the largest infrastruc
risks: If the OpenAI guarantee reduction reflects a broader pattern of hyperscaler and large-customer capex renegotiations rather than a one-off project timing adjustment, near-term revenue visibility could deteriorate — we would need to see corroborating signals from other customers or from NVIDIA's own backlog disclosures.

Concentration risk is highlighted: a single customer commitment at this scale being renegotiated is a reminder that NVIDIA's near-term revenue profile has meaningful dependence on a small number of very large buyers.

Sovereign AI demand is disproportionately concentrated in regions (Middle East, Southeast Asia, parts of Europe) where U.S. export controls could restrict NVIDIA's ability to deliver H100/B200-class hardware, potentially capping addressable sovereign TAM.
Government procurement cycles are slower and more unpredictable than hyperscaler capex, introducing potential lumpiness in recognized revenue if this channel grows.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.last_memo: Alphabet just borrowed $25 billion by issuing bonds to investors, which is notable because this company usually sits on a massive pile of cash and rarely needs to borrow. The bonds range from short-term (due 2028) to very long-term (due 2066), at interest rates between roughly 4.
risks: Use of proceeds is undisclosed; a large acquisition at a full multiple would represent a capital discipline risk inconsistent with the thesis.
If debt is used to fund buybacks at 24x forward earnings, management is prioritizing financial engineering over reinvestment, which would be a credibility yellow flag.
Long-dated tranches (40-year notes at 6.5%) lock in financing cost at elevated rates; if AI capex returns disappoint, this leverage becomes harder to justify.
If AI infrastructure returns disappoint, Alphabet will have permanently increased its capital base and interest burden with limited ability to quickly reverse the commitment.

rows.name: Palantir Tech Inc.
rows.last_memo: Palantir had a strong second quarter and told investors it now expects to make more money this year than it previously guided — a good sign that its AI platform (AIP) is actually being adopted by customers in meaningful ways, not just generating buzz. The stock jumped about 8% on
risks: Stock trading at ~8x the high-case DCF fair value means even strong execution may not prevent multiple compression if macro or sentiment shifts, with no margin of safety for the long-term investor who buys here.

Without the full earnings detail, it is unknown whether the Q2 beat was driven by a large one-time government contract or true broad-based commercial acceleration — the former would be a lower-quality beat.

Karp's public AI warning, while strategically smart, could signal that enterprise AI deployment timelines are stretching, which would delay AIP revenue conversion from bootcamps and pilots to large multi-year contracts.

At 68x trailing sales and ~155x EV/EBITDA, the stock is priced for perfection across a decade — any macro shock, competitor breakthrough, or government budget sequester that interrupts the growth trajectory could cause severe price correction even without fundamental business damage.

rows.name: Shopify Inc.
rows.last_memo: Shopify's stock jumped about 5% today, but there was no news behind it — no earnings, no product announcement, no guidance change. That kind of move on no information is just market noise. The business itself — its millions of merchants, its payments and financial tools, its grow
risks: AI commerce strategy adds execution risk: if Shopify is investing heavily in AI tooling to stay ahead, this may pressure near-term margins or require capital allocation that delays FCF margin expansion.

AI-native commerce platforms (e.g., those building directly on LLM infrastructure) could bypass traditional storefront software entirely — the Q2 call highlights this is on management's radar, suggesting competitive intensity is real.
Valuation-to-fair-value gap (current price ~16x base case fair value) means any miss or guidance cut would cause severe price dislocations, even if the long-term thesis remains intact.
A 17% single-day move compresses the margin of safety further on an already premium valuation, making the stock more sensitive to any future guidance miss.

rows.name: Unitedhealth Group Inc.
rows.last_memo: A group of UnitedHealth shareholders has sued the company's board and executives, claiming they knew for years that the company had serious cybersecurity and governance problems but chose to ignore them. This matters because UnitedHealth's business depends heavily on people trust
risks: Derivative lawsuit discovery may surface internal communications confirming management received and ignored cybersecurity warnings, materially damaging management credibility and triggering regulatory escalation.

Congressional or HHS investigations could be accelerated by the lawsuit's governance allegations, potentially resulting in mandated security standards or capital set-asides that increase operating costs.
Counterparties (large employers, CMS) may cite governance allegations in contract renegotiations or competitive RFPs, creating incremental churn risk in an otherwise sticky customer base.
D&O liability exposure and cyber insurance premiums are likely to increase regardless of lawsuit outcome, representing a structural cost headwind.

rows.name: Tesla Inc.
rows.last_memo: Tesla has started letting its own employees ride in its self-driving Cybercab taxis in Austin, Texas, which is the clearest sign yet that the robotaxi program is actually moving toward real-world use rather than just existing as a demo. This is genuinely good news for the thesis,
risks: A high-profile safety incident during the Austin employee pilot — even a minor one — could trigger regulatory scrutiny that delays or blocks the public launch, disproportionately damaging the AV narrative given how much of the valuation depends on it.

Austin as a single-city pilot may reveal scalability constraints (geofencing, weather, edge cases) that make the path to national deployment longer and more capital-intensive than current investor assumptions.
Competitive pressure from Waymo's already-commercial multi-city operations means Tesla is entering a market where the benchmark is live, paying customers — not internal benchmarks.

Waymo's demonstrated willingness to absorb extreme import costs to scale its fleet signals that well-capitalized rivals will compete aggressively on autonomous deployment regardless of near-term economics, potentially delaying Tesla's window to establish robotaxi network effects.

rows.name: AST SpaceMobile Inc.
rows.last_memo: AST SpaceMobile's Q2 2026 earnings call was flagged as important to review, which it absolutely is for this company — but the actual content of that call was never provided. For a pre-profit satellite startup where every quarter is a test of whether the technology and business mo
risks: Information gap risk: the committee is operating without Q2 2026 results, which means any position sizing or conviction adjustment is being made without the most recent execution data — itself a procedural risk for an early-stage, milestone-driven holding.
Test authorization does not guarantee commercial spectrum rights; the FCC could impose conditions or deny full commercial licensing even after successful testing.
If 800 MHz testing reveals performance shortfalls in real-world conditions, it could reset market expectations that have been pricing in technological success.

Q2 earnings miss, combined with FCF of -$1.8B TTM and accelerating cash burn trend (-$0.21B to -$1.19B over four years), raises the risk that the financing runway is shorter than the timeline to cash-flow-positive operations — the 10-Q cash position and updated capex guidance must be reviewed urgently.
